review_candidates.title: National Consultant - Baseline Profiling and Capacity Needs Assessment
review_candidates.description: Job Description Background/Context UN Women is the United Nations entity dedicated to gender equality and the empowerment of women. As the lead United Nations agency on gender equality, UN Women works to eliminate discrimination against women and girls; empower women; and achieve equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action, and peace and security. In Tanzania, UN Women works closely with the Government of Tanzania, civil society organizations, development partners, and communities to advance women's leadership and participation, women economic empowerment , end violence against women and girls, strengthen gender-responsive governance systems, and promote women's meaningful engagement in peace and security processes. The Women, Peace and Security (WPS) agenda, established through United Nations Security Council Resolution 1325 and subsequent resolutions, recognizes the critical role of women in conflict prevention, peacebuilding, conflict resolution, humanitarian action, and recovery. For Tanzania, UN Women has partnered with the Ministry of Community Development, Gender, Women and Special Groups (Mainland), the Ministry of Community Development, Gender, Elderly and Children (Zanzibar), and other stakeholders to advance the WPS agenda and strengthen institutional frameworks that promote women's participation, leadership, protection, and access to decision-making in peace and security processes. These efforts culminated in the development of Tanzania's first National Action Plan on Women, Peace and Security (TNAP-WPS) 2025-2029, which provides the national framework for advancing gender-responsive peace, security, and resilience interventions across the country. The United Republic of Tanzania adopted its first TNAP WPS through official launch in August 2025, outlining national priorities across the four WPS pillars: Prevention, Participation, Protection, and Relief & Recovery. The TNAP identifies eight priority regions Kigoma, Mtwara, Lindi, Arusha, Mara, Tanga, Unguja Mjini, and Pemba Kusini where implementation will begin due to contextual vulnerabilities, humanitarian pressures, cross border dynamics, and opportunities for strengthening localized peace and security mechanisms. To accelerate implementation, the Government validated a One-Year Implementation Plan (2025–2026) designed to kick start operationalization of the TNAP in these regions. The plan focuses on interventions requiring strengthened institutional capacity, gender responsive systems, coordinated WPS structures, and improved linkages between national and local actors. Lessons generated during this first year will inform the progressive roll out of TNAP WPS implementation across the rest of the country. Localization of the TNAP-WPS aligns with national development and governance frameworks, including FYDP IV, which prioritizes human capital development, gender equality, social cohesion, and resilient governance systems, and DIRA 2050, which envisions a peaceful, secure, and inclusive Tanzania built on strong institutions and equitable participation. In Tanzania Mainland, implementation of the TNAP-WPS will also be aligned with the emerging Jamii Agenda 2050, which emphasizes inclusive interventions, meaningful community participation, and effective use of resources to strengthen social welfare, social cohesion, and community resilience. The integrated baseline profiling and capacity needs assessment is therefore an opportunity to examine the extent to which the TNAP-WPS, Jamii Agenda 2050, and other relevant national frameworks are reflected within regional and local planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting mechanisms, while identifying opportunities to strengthen coherence and synergies across these initiatives. This assessment is funded by the Embassy of Ireland through the Joint Initiative to Strengthen National and Development Partners' Gender Equality Coordination Mechanisms, which supports enhanced implementation, coordination, monitoring, and reporting of Tanzania's national gender equality commitments, including the National Gender and Women Development Policy, the Tanzania Generation Equality Platform (TGEP), the National Plan of Action to End Violence Against Women and Children (NPA-VAWC II), and the TNAP-WPS. As part of this support, the Joint Initiative is financing integrated baseline profiling and capacity needs assessment to generate evidence for effective localization and operationalization of the TNAP-WPS. To support effective implementation , UN Women in collaboration with the Ministry of Community Development, Gender, Women and Special Groups (Mainland), the Ministry of Community Development, Gender, Elderly and Children (Zanzibar), and intends to engage a qualified consultant to conduct an integrated baseline profiling and capacity needs assessment across the eight priority regions. This combined assignment will generate a comprehensive picture of the current WPS landscape, institutional readiness, community structures, gender responsive systems, and coordination mechanisms, while identifying gaps and proposing actionable capacity strengthening strategies. Organizational setting, reporting and collaborators. The consultant will be reporting to Programme manager and will be supported by Programme Analyst who will be the point of contact on the contract and payment issues. Supervisory Arrangements The consultant will report to UN Women Tanzania, with technical oversight provided by the WPS National Technical committee and relevant ministries. UN Women and government partners will provide background documents, facilitate access to stakeholders, and support field coordination throughout the assignment. Travel to the eight priority regions may be required and will be subject to approval by UN Women. The consultant’s performance will be assessed based on timeliness, quality of deliverables, analytical rigor, stakeholder engagement, and clarity of reporting. Description Of Responsibilities/ Scope Of Work General objectives of the assignment To conduct a combined baseline profiling and capacity needs assessment of institutions, actors, systems, and community structures responsible for implementing the TNAP‑WPS in priority regions, and to produce actionable recommendations and a capacity‑strengthening plan that supports effective localization and sustained implementation of the WPS agenda. Specific Objectives Baseline Profiling Objectives Establish baseline data on WPS‑related structures, systems, actors, and interventions in the eight priority regions. Document existing peacebuilding, protection, humanitarian, and gender‑equality mechanisms at regional, district, ward, village/shehia levels. Map WPS actors, networks, committees, peace clubs, security organs, and community structures. Identify contextual factors, conflict drivers, protection risks, and gender‑specific vulnerabilities relevant to TNAP‑WPS implementation. Capacity Needs Assessment Objectives Assesses institutional, technical, human resource, coordination, and operational capacities of WPS‑related structures. Identify gaps in knowledge, skills, systems, tools, and resources required to implement TNAP‑WPS activities. Assess gender mainstreaming capacity within security organs, LGAs, humanitarian response structures, and community protection mechanisms. Propose a capacity‑building plan including training modules, institutional strengthening measures, coordination mechanisms, and resource requirements. Provide recommendations for integrating WPS into local development plans, sectoral strategies, and LGA operational systems, aligned with FYDP IV and DIRA 2050. Scope of Work/Duties and Responsibilities The consultant will work closely with UN Women, the WPS National Steering Committee, regional authorities, and local government structures in the eight priority regions. Document Review TNAP‑WPS and One‑Year Implementation Plan Regional security profiles LGA development plans Gender policies and guidelines Existing WPS initiatives Regional development of blueprints and relevant sectoral plans at the regional level. Training curricula, SOPs, and tools used by peace and security structures Baseline Profiling Map WPS actors, networks, committees, peace clubs, security organs, humanitarian actors, and community structures. Document existing systems, coordination mechanisms, gender desks, peace committees, and protection services. Profile contextual risks, conflict dynamics, cross‑border issues, SGBV trends, and humanitarian pressures. Establish baseline indicators aligned with TNAP‑WPS results framework. Institutional Capacity Assessment Assess the capacity of regional and district security committees to coordinate and implement WPS‑related interventions, including their operational structures, mandates, and existing mechanisms for conflict prevention, early warning, and response. Examine the functionality and effectiveness of gender desks within the police and Local Government Authorities (LGAs), with emphasis on case management, survivor‑centred approaches, referral pathways, and linkages with justice and protection systems. Review the establishment, activities, and sustainability of peace clubs in schools, including their contribution to peace education, youth engagement, early warning, and community cohesion. Assess the institutional strength, outreach, and coordination capacity of women’s networks including AWLN, TPF‑NET, SHIVYAWATA, NACOPHA, Sisters Without Borders, and others operating within the priority regions and evaluate their role in advancing WPS commitments. Evaluate the role and influence of religious and traditional leaders, civil society organizations (CSOs), women’s rights organizations (WROs), refugee‑hosting institutions in Kigoma, disaster management committees, and border management and migration centers in promoting gender‑responsive peacebuilding, conflict mediation, humanitarian response, and protection of women and girls, including their operational readiness and coordination with national and regional structures. Review and analyze Regional Development Plans and relevant district and local government plans in the priority regions to assess the extent to which WPS priorities are integrated into subnational development planning. Stakeholder Consultations Conduct Key Informant Interviews (KIIs), Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), and technical consultations with Regional Commissioners and Local Government Authorities to assess institutional readiness, coordination gaps, and the overall enabling environment for localized WPS implementation. Engage security organs including the police, Tanzania People’s Defence Forces (TPDF), prisons, and immigration services to examine their mandates, operational roles, and gender‑responsive capacities in advancing TNAP‑WPS priorities across prevention, protection, and response functions. Consult community leaders to capture local perspectives on conflict drivers, protection risks, social norms, and community‑based peace-building mechanisms that influence WPS outcomes at grassroots level. Engage women’s rights organizations and youth groups to document their contributions, challenges, and opportunities for strengthening inclusive participation, early warning, peacebuilding, and community resilience within WPS structures. Consult humanitarian actors and peacebuilding committees to assess coordination mechanisms, protection services, gender‑responsive humanitarian capacities, and operational gaps affecting localized implementation of the WPS agenda. Skills and Knowledge Gap Analysis Assess gaps in gender mainstreaming across institutions at the regional level responsible for WPS implementation, including limitations in gender‑responsive planning, budgeting, analysis, and service delivery, and the extent to which staff understand and apply gender principles in their daily functions. Identify gaps in conflict prevention capacities, including weaknesses in early warning systems, mediation and negotiation skills, community‑based conflict resolution approaches, and the ability of institutions to anticipate, analyze, and respond to emerging risks. Examine gaps in Sexual and Gender‑Based Violence (SGBV) response capacities, focusing on survivor‑centered approaches, referral pathways, case management, coordination with justice and health systems, and the availability of trained personnel and appropriate tools. Assess knowledge and skills gaps in peacebuilding, humanitarian response, leadership, and WPS coordination, including inclusive dialogue facilitation, social cohesion promotion, protection‑focused humanitarian action, women’s leadership in peace and security structures, and institutional capacities for reporting, monitoring, and alignment with TNAP‑WPS priorities. Capacity‑Building Strategy Development Develop training modules aligned with TNAP‑WPS priorities, addressing identified gaps in gender mainstreaming, conflict prevention, protection, peacebuilding, and humanitarian response. Recommend institutional strengthening measures to enhance coordination, accountability, and operational effectiveness of WPS‑related structures at national and sub‑national levels. Propose coordination and reporting mechanisms that improve linkages between regional, district, ward, and community‑level WPS actors, ensuring alignment with national frameworks. Identify resource requirements, potential partners, and opportunities for leveraging existing programmes to support sustainable capacity‑building and long‑term institutional strengthening. S/N Deliverable Timeline) 1 Draft inception report (workplan, methodology, tools, stakeholder map) 7 Days 2 Final inception report (validated tools, sampling, analytical framework) 3 Days 3 Zero draft baseline & capacity assessment report 18 Days 4 First draft & stakeholder presentation 5 Days 5 Final report & capacity‑building plan 7 Days Co

review_candidates.title: Monitoring and Reporting Analyst, NOB, TA, Kyiv, Ukraine
review_candidates.description: Job Description Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works in Ukraine with the government, parliament, and civil society for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. UN Women works closely with the UN Country Team and Humanitarian Country Team in integration of women’s rights and gender equality in all spheres of UN work. Since the beginning of the Russian military full-scale invasion on 24 February 2022, Ukraine is rapidly emerging as one of the world’s most complex emergencies where w omen and men, girls and boys, in all their diversities, have been profoundly impacted. During 2022-2026, at least 5,489 women have been killed and 356 girls. Additionally, 18,437 women have been injured and 1,290 girls [1] . 2.91 million people predominantly women and girls are at high risk of gender-based violence [2] . In 2026, the impacts of Russia’s full-scale invasion are multiplying - at least 372 civilians were killed and 2,349 injured in Ukraine only in August 2026, marking the second highest month of civilians killed and injured in 2026 since July 2026 (448 killed; 2,675 injured) [3] . The relentless, systematic attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure and services, including energy, transport, health and education facilities have a severe and growing effect on women, with death, mutilation, severe bodily and psychological trauma, displacement, gender-based violence including conflict related sexual violence (CRSV), human trafficking, loss of livelihoods and economic opportunities as detailed in the statistics below. These attacks are grave violations of human rights and international humanitarian law. Since 2016, UN Women in Ukraine has supported its government and non-government counterparts and stakeholders to advance gender equality and women’s empowerment (GEWE). These efforts have been strengthened to meet the urgent and deep needs caused by the ongoing humanitarian crisis. Under its 2025-2029 Strategic Note, UN Women in Ukraine aims to ensure that more women and girls, including those at the greatest risk of being left behind, lead, influence and benefit from gender responsive humanitarian action, governance, recovery, rights and economic growth. Among others, c ivil society, and particularly women’s organizations in Ukraine, are in the front-line to deliver immediate humanitarian assistance to displaced women and girls. Women’s groups and civil society organizations have been quick to react to the immediate priorities of their communities but face many challenges as they attempt to provide support to large numbers of internally displaced people, host-communities and those directly affected by violence and insecurity. As one of the worldwide biggest supporters for local and grassroots women’s civil society leaders and their organizations in conflict and crisis settings , the United Nations Women's Peace and Humanitarian Fund (WPHF), with the technical support of UN Women, in 2022 has activated its emergency response for Ukraine by supporting local women's rights organizations in Ukraine and Moldova on the frontlines of the response to the needs and displacement of women and girls. Reporting to Programme Specialist (WPHF) and under the overall supervision of the Head of Programmes [RS1] , the Monitoring and Reporting Analyst will provide support to WPHF team and the Ukraine Country Office in incorporating monitoring and reporting into programme formulation as well as will perform monitoring, reporting and evaluation services to track and report the results against the CO Strategic Note and UN Women Strategic Plan targets to internal and external audiences. [1] HRMM, Protection of civilians in Armed Conflict. August, 2026 , p.4. [2] OCHA - Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan Ukraine - Humanitarian Programme Cycle 2026 ,January 2026, p.3. [3] HRMM, Protection of civilians in Armed Conflict July 2026 , p.5. Key Functions and Accountabilities: Facilitate and substantively contribute to the incorporation of monitoring and reporting into programme formulation Facilitate and substantively contribute to the development of monitoring indicators, monitoring calendars, and field monitoring plans and quality assurance processes; Include inputs from relevant evaluation findings, conclusions and recommendations into programme formulation; Contribute to annual work plan monitoring, reviews and reporting; Provide technical support to partners in developing Performance Monitoring Frameworks (PMFs), systems and plans, and Baseline Surveys; Facilitate the clearance of donor agreements and Programme Cooperation Agreements with CO. Contribute substantively to the monitoring and tracking of results against country/ regional level targets and UN Women Strategic Plan Coordinate with Programme Team to ensure that data collection and analysis from field visits are coordinated and standardized across programmes; Monitor data from partners on a quarterly basis and provide substantive inputs to regular management briefs to inform decision making; Visit partners, along with the Programme Team, to support monitoring of results and planning processes as required; Monitor the spending of donor funds and other programme expenditures and disbursements; Draft and monitor the CO Monitoring, Evaluation, and Research Plan. Facilitate the reporting of results to internal (Senior Management) and external (Executive Board, Donors) audiences Facilitate the process of the CO meeting internal and external reporting requirements and deadlines, including annual reporting process; Draft donor and programme reports (both narrative and financial); Identify relevant evaluation findings, conclusions and recommendations and input them into programme reporting; Review progress reports submitted by partners and provide feedback to improve quality and timeliness of reporting; Collect and maintain data for country, regional and global corporate reports, mid-term reviews, and final evaluations. Provide technical support to the CO in the implementation the UN Women Evaluation Policy Coordinate the implementation of UN Women’s Evaluation plan in the CO; Provide guidance to programme staff on evaluations; Ensure communication between the CO and RO regarding Evaluations; Coordinate the completion of management’s response to the UN Women Global Accountability and Tracking of Evaluation Use (GATE). Contribute to knowledge building and capacity building Identify and disseminate good practices, lessons and knowledge, as identified through programme implementation, monitoring and evaluation activities; Contribute to the development of capacity development tools, including training materials and packages; Facilitate capacity building opportunities for staff and partners in the country in the areas of Results Based Management (RBM), Monitoring and Evaluation; Promote the awareness and understanding of the shared responsibility of Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) among all staff members through communication, training, learning and development activities. The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation. Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: N/A Recruitment Qualifications Education and certification: Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Political or Social Science, Economics, International Development Studies, Gender/Women's Studies is required. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. A project/programme management certification (such as PMP®, PRINCE2®, or MSP®) would be an added advantage. Experience: At least 2 years of progressively responsible experience at the national or international level in monitoring and reporting of development projects/programmes is required. Experience in the United Nations systems in desirable. Field experience is desirable. Experience in the usage of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and spreadsheet and database packages, experience in handling of web-based management systems is required. Experience in the use of a modern web-based ERP System, preferably Oracle Cloud, is desirable. Language Requirements: Fluency in English and Ukrainian is required. Knowledge of another official UN language is desirable (French, Arabic, Chinese, Russian or Spanish). Knowledge of dashboards creation and activities/objects geographical mapping is an asset. Competencies : Core Values: Integrity; Professionalism; Respect for Diversity. Core Competencies: Awareness and Sensitivity Regarding Gender Issues; Accountability; Creative Problem Solving; Effective Communication; Inclusive Collaboration; Stakeholder Engagement; Leading by Example. Please visit this link for more information on UN Women’s Values and Competencies Framework: Functional Competencies: Good knowledge of programme formulation and implementation and Results Based Management Good knowledge of monitoring and evaluation, evaluation design, data collection and analysis, and reporting Ability to synthesize program performance data and produce analytical reports Good analytical and report writing skills Knowledge of UN programme management systems Statements : In July 2010, the United Nations General Assembly created UN Women, the United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women. The creation of UN Women came about as part of the UN reform agenda, bringing together resources and mandates for greater impact. It merges and builds on the important work of four previously distinct parts of the UN system (DAW, OSAGI, INSTRAW and UNIFEM), which focused exclusively on gender equality and women's empowerment. Diversity and inclusion: At UN Women, we are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. UN Women recruits, employs, trains, compensates, and promotes regardless of race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, ability, national origin, or any other basis covered by appropriate law. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, competence, integrity and organizational need. If you need any reasonable accommodation to support your participation in the recruitment and selection process, please include this information in your application. UN Women has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UN Women, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination. All selected candidates will be expected to adhere to UN Women’s policies and procedures and the standards of conduct expected of UN Women personnel and will therefore undergo rigorous reference and background checks. (Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check.) Note: Applicants must ensure that all sections of the application form, including the sections on education and employment history, are completed. If all sections are not completed the application may be disqualified from the recruitment and selection process .

review_candidates.description: Bedrijf Anton Civiel & Infra Dienstverband Fulltime Locatie Heerhugowaard Werk jij graag buiten en zie je direct resultaat van je werk in de omgeving om je heen? Heb jij ervaring op de kraan, houd je van overzicht en voel je je thuis in de civiele infra? Dan is deze functie als Mobiele Kraanmachinist bij Anton Civiel & Infra precies wat je zoekt. In deze rol werk je met een moderne Hitachi mobiele kraan van 18 ton, voorzien van alle gemakken en GPS, aan uiteenlopende projecten in de grond-, weg- en waterbouw. Denk aan rioolvervanging, herinrichting van woonwijken, kabel- en leidingwerk en het bouw- en woonrijp maken van gebieden. Jij bent degene die het werk letterlijk in beweging zet. Met je mobiele kraan ben je overal op het project te vinden. Je graaft en hijst, en je zorgt er ook voor dat materialen op het juiste moment op de juiste plek liggen. Daardoor heb je als geen ander overzicht over de bouw en ben je de ogen en oren van de uitvoerder. Je werkt nauw samen met grondwerkers, uitvoerders en collega-machinisten aan projecten in Noord-Holland en omgeving. Eén ding staat altijd vast: jij zorgt voor strak en veilig kraanwerk waarop het team verder kan bouwen. Meer weten over deze vacature? Voor deze functie zoeken we een ervaren of leergierige kraanmachinist die graag in de civiele infra werkt. Jij houdt van buiten werken, hebt gevoel voor techniek en weet hoe je een kraan beheerst in drukke of krappe omgevingen. Daarnaast zul je ook zo nu en dan naast de kraan staan. Je hebt een opleiding tot Kraanmachinist of voldoende ervaring als kraanmachinist in de GWW Rijbewijs B, E is een pré VCA-certificaat of bereid dit te behalen Ervaring met een mobiele kraan, of met een rupskraan vanaf midi-formaat Kennis van tekening lezen en maatvoering is een pré Je bent bereid om, wanneer het werk daarom vraagt, ook naast je collega mee te werken op de grond naast de kraan Je werkt nauwkeurig, veilig en denkt in oplossingen Je bent flexibel en gewend om in teamverband te werken Twijfel je of je volledig past? Geen probleem. We gaan graag met je in gesprek. In deze rol ben jij dagelijks actief met jouw mobiele kraan op diverse civiele en infra projecten. Je zorgt voor nauwkeurig en veilig graaf- en hijswerk en houdt de logistiek op het project draaiende, zodat je collega’s niets tekortkomen. Omdat we werken in kleine, hechte ploegen, ben je niet alleen machinist, maar ook onderdeel van het uitvoerende team. Dat betekent dat je waar nodig ook uit de kraan stapt om je collega’s te ondersteunen bij grondwerk, maatvoering of het begeleiden van werkzaamheden. Juist die afwisseling maakt het werk veelzijdig en praktisch. Graafwerk & grondverzet: uitvoeren van sleufwerk, ontgravingen en aanvullen van grond. Logistiek op het project: in overleg met de uitvoerder en voormannen zorg je dat materialen tijdig en op de juiste plek over het project worden verplaatst. Zie je een slimmere aanpak? Dan horen we dat graag. Riool- en kabelwerk: ondersteunen bij het aanleggen en vervangen van rioleringen en kabels & leidingen, inclusief nauwkeurig werken op hoogte en diepte. Civiele werkzaamheden: voorbereiden van cunetten, uitgraven van bouw- en woonrijp terrein en assisteren bij het plaatsen van putten, kolken en prefab elementen. Meewerken in de ploeg: waar nodig stap je uit de kraan om grondwerkers te ondersteunen, maatvoering te controleren of hand- en spandiensten te verrichten op het project. Nauwkeurig werken: werken met GPS-machinebesturing of maatvoering op tekening, en zorgen dat het werk exact volgens ontwerp wordt uitgevoerd. Samenwerken & veiligheid: intensief samenwerken met grondwerkers en uitvoerders, signaleren van afwijkingen en altijd werken volgens VCA- en KAM-richtlijnen. Jij bent een machinist die vooruitdenkt, netjes werkt en oog heeft voor veiligheid, planning en kwaliteit. Met een jong en energiek team realiseren wij samen diverse bouwprojecten binnen de grond-, weg- en waterbouw, renovatie en herinrichting. Elk project benaderen we met een frisse blik en een integrale visie, waarbij we alles begeleiden, van ontwerp en engineering tot uitvoering en eindoplevering. We houden ons bezig met uitdagende projecten, van kleinschalige initiatieven tot aan megaprojecten, want voor ons is niets te gek! Samen zetten we ons in voor de ontwikkeling van onze eigen omgeving. Benieuwd naar de projecten waar wij aan werken? Kijk dan eens op: Projecten Anton Civiel & Infra is onderdeel van de Anton Groep. Een nuchter Noord-Hollands bouwbedrijf gevestigd in Obdam. Onze groep bestaat uit diverse bedrijven, allen actief in de bouw en techniek sector met elk haar eigen specialisme. Dit stelt ons in staat om toegang te hebben tot alle benodigde expertise en om samen te werken aan een alomvattend eindresultaat. Dagelijks zetten zo’n 200 collega’s zich in voor uitdagende projecten. Bij Anton Civiel & Infra geloven we dat werk meer is dan alleen een baan. Je werkt met modern materieel aan uitdagende civiele infra projecten in jouw regio, samen met collega’s die voor elkaar klaarstaan. We bieden je een nuchtere en professionele werkomgeving met korte lijnen, veel eigen verantwoordelijkheid en de ruimte om jezelf verder te ontwikkelen. Daarnaast Bieden Wij Een salaris conform de bouw en infra CAO naar gelang je ervaring. (Indicatie €3.300 – €3.700,-) 30 vakantiedagen + 13 dagen per jaar uitbetaald in salaris die je extra kunt terugkopen. Goede secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden volgens de cao Bouw en Infra. Een platte organisatie met korte lijnen en veel ruimte voor eigen initiatief en ontwikkeling. Gezellige teamuitjes en personeelsactiviteiten. Toegang tot sportieve activiteiten en een voordelig sportabonnement. En dat is nog lang niet alles! Ontdek wat werken bij de Anton Groep nog meer te bieden heeft op Ook dit is Anton – Anton Groep Klaar voor een nieuwe stap? Solliciteer op deze vacature! Klinkt dit als jouw volgende stap? The power is in your hands to define what success looks like and where you want to take your career. It's not just about what we do, but about who we become on along the way. We are much more than a brand here. We are a way of life, a mindset. Join us. A Day In The Life As a Field Sales Representative at Monster Energy, you'll be at the forefront of energizing and amplifying bottler relationships, turning each interaction into a powerhouse of potential. Your mission is to educate and inspire partner representatives to forge new trails in distribution, amp up volume in existing accounts, and execute inspiring strategies at both chain and local account levels within your dynamic territory. You'll be the driving force behind bottler business results in your assigned geography, spearheading the success of company initiatives. This includes invigorating bottler sales and execution, while rolling out impactful national and local marketing programs that capture market share and smash budget targets. Your journey will be marked by exceptional bottler management skills, unparalleled market execution abilities, and the talent to forge strong, lasting relationships. Embrace the challenge and lead with the unstoppable energy of Monster! The Impact You'll Make Train Bottler Sales Representatives on product knowledge, sales methodologies, and marketing and sales promotions by influencing bottler actions at multiple levels of their organization. Accomplish through partnership ride-alongs in retail outlets, sales presentations within the bottler's facilities, 'huddle' calls with bottler reps, and team calls with both internal and external partners. Sell at retail (outlet level) aligned against quarterly strategic initiatives focused on innovation, distribution, displays, and cold/ambient equipment placements. Accomplish in conjunction with bottler partners in the trade together or through influencing bottler actions. Complete comprehension and utilization of all Monster Energy Company tools (CRM) and capabilities to maximize productivity and results in their assigned market including but not limited to surveys, training tools, sales data software, asset allocation, and internal social platforms. Participate in business unit crew drives, market audits, company meetings and events, sampling initiatives, and local retail meetings. Duties would include set-up, tear-down, customer hosting, sales presentations and additional responsibilities. Who You Are Prefer a bachelor's degree in the field of -- Business Administration or related field of study Experience Desired: Minimum 1 year of experience in Sales or Marketing Additional Experience Desired: Minimum 1 year of experience in Beverage or Consumer packaged goods (CPG) field Computer Skills Desired: Computer operating skills in and outside of an office environment to include handheld devices Preferred Certifications: Maintain an acceptable driving record in order to be covered by the company’s insurance carrier Monster Energy provides competitive total compensation. review_candidates.title: Engenheiro de dados
review_candidates.description: Descrição da vaga Buscamos um(a) Engenheiro(a) de Dados para atuar em projetos estratégicos de negócios, tecnologia e dados de cliente do setor bancário, contribuindo para a construção, evolução e sustentação de soluções de integração, processamento e disponibilização de dados. O profissional será responsável por desenvolver pipelines de dados eficientes, escaláveis e seguros, garantindo a qualidade, integridade e disponibilidade das informações utilizadas pelas diferentes áreas de negócio. Além do conhecimento técnico, buscamos um profissional com perfil consultivo, boa comunicação e capacidade de interagir diretamente com stakeholders das áreas de negócio , compreendendo suas necessidades e traduzindo-as em soluções tecnológicas. A atuação ocorrerá em um ambiente dinâmico, com grande volume de informações, arquitetura distribuída e utilização de tecnologias modernas, especialmente no ecossistema AWS. Responsabilidades e atribuições Projetar, desenvolver, implementar e manter pipelines de dados para extração, transformação, integração e disponibilização de informações. Desenvolver processos de ETL/ELT, garantindo eficiência, escalabilidade, rastreabilidade e qualidade dos dados. Atuar na integração de diferentes fontes de dados, incluindo bancos relacionais, APIs, arquivos estruturados e semiestruturados. Desenvolver scripts e aplicações utilizando Python e SQL, com foco em extração, tratamento, transformação e manipulação de dados. Construir e otimizar soluções de processamento de dados em ambientes cloud, preferencialmente AWS. Participar da definição e evolução de arquiteturas de dados, considerando Data Lakes, Data Warehouses e soluções analíticas. Implementar mecanismos de monitoramento, observabilidade e tratamento de falhas nos pipelines. Aplicar boas práticas de segurança, governança, qualidade e proteção de dados, considerando os requisitos do ambiente financeiro. Identificar oportunidades de automação e melhoria contínua nos processos de engenharia de dados. Realizar levantamento e análise de requisitos diretamente com áreas de negócio, compreendendo processos, necessidades e objetivos. Traduzir requisitos funcionais e necessidades de negócio em especificações técnicas e soluções de dados. Interagir com equipes de desenvolvimento, arquitetura, infraestrutura, segurança e analytics. Documentar soluções, fluxos de dados, regras de transformação e integrações desenvolvidas. Apoiar análises técnicas e funcionais para identificação de inconsistências e oportunidades de melhoria nos dados. Requisitos e qualificações Experiência sólida em desenvolvimento utilizando Python para processamento, manipulação e integração de dados. Conhecimento avançado em SQL, incluindo consultas complexas, joins, procedures e otimização de queries. Experiência com bibliotecas Python para tratamento e processamento de dados, como Pandas e PySpark. Experiência com integração de dados por meio de APIs REST, arquivos JSON, CSV e formatos como Parquet. Experiência na construção e manutenção de pipelines ETL/ELT. Conhecimento em modelagem de dados relacional e dimensional. Experiência com bancos de dados relacionais e soluções de armazenamento analítico. Conhecimento de arquiteturas Data Lake e Data Warehouse. Experiência com processamento de grandes volumes de dados. Conhecimento em mecanismos de orquestração e agendamento de pipelines. Familiaridade com conceitos de qualidade, catalogação, linhagem e governança de dados. Experiência no levantamento de requisitos funcionais e técnicos junto a usuários e áreas de negócio. Capacidade de compreender processos de negócio e identificar necessidades relacionadas ao consumo e tratamento de dados. Habilidade para transformar demandas de negócio em soluções técnicas estruturadas. Experiência na documentação de requisitos, regras de negócio e fluxos de integração. Capacidade de conduzir reuniões técnicas e funcionais com diferentes stakeholders. Diferenciais técnicos Apache Airflow para orquestração de pipelines. PySpark para processamento distribuído e manipulação de grandes volumes de dados. Python aplicado a engenharia e ciência de dados. Pandas e Numpy para manipulação e análise de dados. SQL avançado para consultas, modelagem e otimização. Experiência com AWS Cloud, incluindo: AWS Glue (ETL/ELT) Amazon Redshift (data warehouse) Consultas em dados armazenados no Amazon S3 Experiência com modelagem dimensional (fatos, dimensões, modelo estrela). Vivência com pipelines de dados e boas práticas de governança. Desejáveis Experiência no setor financeiro Familiaridade com ferramentas de visualização (Power BI, Tableau, Looker). Conhecimento de versionamento (Git) e boas práticas de desenvolvimento. Noções de qualidade e catalogação de dados (Data Quality, Data Catalog). Transformamos mundos sonhados em trajetórias reais.🧡🚀 Aqui somos #SangueLaranja! Estamos há 17 anos no mercado, lado a lado com nossos clientes, proporcionando experiências transformadoras. Somos um ecossistema de tecnologia e inovação, com expansão global; Além do Brasil estamos presentes na Europa e Reino Unido com escritórios em Portugal, Londres, Dubai e Holanda. 🌎 F de Formação: acreditamos na prática da cultura do compartilhamento, no senso de comunidade, e que o conhecimento tem o poder da transformação! Possuímos iniciativas, e ações sociais, que promovem o desenvolvimento, como a comunidade tech Orange Juice, o Programa de Formação, nossa escola de liderança e diversas parcerias com ONGs e Edtechs. Na FCamara todos são bem-vindos, para nós, Diversidade, Respeito e Ética, são elementos inegociáveis e fazem parte do nosso DNA. E aí, está pronto para fazer parte de um time incrível e ser protagonista da própria história?

review_candidates.description: Company Description Måne Energi AS delivers engineering solutions across the full energy project lifecycle, from early concept studies to detailed engineering, construction management, commissioning, and safe system handover. The company focuses on Safety & Automation Systems, Instrument & Electrical Engineering, Process Engineering & Optimization, System Commissioning & Testing, and Industrial Cybersecurity & OT Protection. Måne Energi AS works closely with clients to improve operational performance while maintaining high safety standards. The organization is committed to sustainable, value-driven solutions that support a robust and future-oriented energy sector. Position Summary Måne Energi is seeking an Electrical Engineer to support the development and delivery of electrical engineering solutions across energy, industrial, and infrastructure projects. The successful candidate will contribute throughout the project lifecycle, from concept development and design through procurement support, construction follow-up, commissioning, and operational improvements. The role requires sound engineering judgment, attention to detail, and the ability to collaborate effectively within multidisciplinary project teams. Key Responsibilities Develop electrical engineering deliverables in accordance with project requirements and applicable standards. Prepare technical specifications, calculations, reports, and design documentation. Design and review electrical power distribution systems. Participate in equipment sizing, selection, and technical evaluations. Support preparation and review of electrical layouts, schematics, and system diagrams. Coordinate technical interfaces with automation, instrumentation, telecom, process, and mechanical disciplines. Review supplier and vendor documentation. Participate in design reviews, technical workshops, and client meetings. Support installation, testing, commissioning, and troubleshooting activities. Promote safety, quality, reliability, and maintainability in engineering solutions. Onshore/Offshore survey/FAT. Estimating of cost and weight in a multi discipline environment Qualifications Required Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in: Electrical Engineering Energy Engineering Power Systems Engineering Automation Engineering Or a related engineering discipline Strong understanding of electrical engineering principles. Ability to interpret technical documentation and engineering drawings. Structured and analytical working approach. Effective communication and collaboration skills. Proficiency in written and spoken English. Experience with ATEX requirements and ATEX certified equipment. Preferred Experience in one or more of the following areas: Low-voltage (LV) systems High-voltage (HV) systems Power distribution systems Variable speed drives Motor control systems Emergency power systems Industrial electrical installations Renewable energy projects Offshore or onshore energy facilities Knowledge of: Electrical design standards Protection and control systems Earthing and bonding systems Electrical safety principles Power system studies Energy efficiency and sustainability practices NORSOK and relevant standards/regulatives for NCS. Norwegian language proficiency (written and/or verbal) is considered an advantage and may be beneficial for communication with customers, suppliers, authorities, and project stakeholders. Personal Attributes We seek individuals who: Demonstrate integrity and professionalism. Take ownership of their work and commitments. Communicate clearly and respectfully. Collaborate effectively across disciplines. Continuously seek improvement and learning opportunities. Approach challenges with a practical and solution-oriented mindset. Contribute to a positive, safe, and inclusive work environment. What We Offer Opportunities to work on meaningful engineering and EPCM projects. Exposure to multidisciplinary project environments. Flexible and collaborative working culture. Professional development and continuous learning opportunities. A company built on trust, accountability, innovation, and engineering excellence. A healthy work-life balance that supports both professional success and personal well-being. Success in This Role A successful Electrical Engineer at Måne Energi: Delivers technically sound and practical solutions. Maintains high standards of quality and safety. Builds positive working relationships with clients and colleagues. Supports efficient project execution from design to operation. Contributes to long-term value creation for customers and stakeholders. Måne Energi Culture Statement We are looking for engineers who combine technical competence with ownership, integrity, and a passion for solving real-world challenges. At Måne Energi, success is built through collaboration, continuous learning, and a commitment to delivering reliable engineering solutions.
